provenance.original: TSA uses historical data from the LEO Flying Armed Application which vets and stores all National Law Enforcement Telecommunications System messages (known as flying while armed messages) submitted by state, local, and tribal LEOs.  Based on this data, TSA estimates an average annual number of 83,749 responses to this collection.  Each response consists of filling out a short form at the screening checkpoint.  TSA estimates that the time burden for this activity is 4 minute (0.0667 hours).  TSA estimates the average annual hour burden cost to the public to be 5,583 hours per year (16,750 hours over the 3-year period).  Respondents to this collection are state, local, tribal, and territorial LEOs travelling on official business, therefore TSA uses a fully-loaded hourly wage rate of $64.48 to estimate the hour burden cost.  TSA estimates the average annual hour burden cost to the public to be $359,990.  Table 1 summarizes these calculations.

TSA estimates it takes 1 hour to complete and submit a DASSP application, for an annual hour burden of 78 hours (234 over three years). provenance.original: The total annual hour burden of this collection is 43,200 hours.  This equates to 129,600 hours over 3 years (43,200 hours x 3 years).  As TSO candidates can be any member of the public, TSA uses the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) all occupations (00-0000) mean wage rate of $32.66 per hour.  TSA then applies a load factor of 1.4582 to account for non-compensation costs of employment, such as health and retirement benefits.  This results in a fully loaded applicant compensation rate of $47.63.  Multiplying the total annual hour burden (43,200 by the all occupation wage rate ($47.63) results in an annual cost of $2,057,616.  See Table 1 for a summary of these calculations.

provenance.original: TWIC STAs and cards are valid for 5 years from the date of issuance, then must be renewed.  TWIC STA may be renewed online, or in-person at an enrollment center. It takes an average of 11 minutes (5 minutes wait time + 6 minutes to complete renewal application), plus a round trip visit to an enrollment center (44 minutes) for a total of 55 minutes (0.9167 hours) to renew in-person.  TSA estimates 68 percent of renewals will be conducted online, while 32 percent of renewals will be done in-person.  The time burden for renewals is displayed in Table 3.
